title: Define supported Redwood-verified models for Quickstart Templates v1 (RAG + agents)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description: Decide which Redwood-verified models Quickstart Templates v1 should target (chat + embeddings + optional rerank), including default pins, upgrade guidance, and safe fallback policy recommendations that template code/docs will implement.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Publish a v1 supported-model list with pinned identifiers for chat + embeddings (rerank optional) that meet template capability requirements (streaming, tool calling, structured output). 2) Provide default + recommended production tier guidance and an explicit pinning/upgrade story. 3) Provide a conservative fallback policy (when to fallback; when not to) that DevEx can implement uniformly in Python/TS templates. 4) Confirm how these pins should be represented in `.env.example` and docs (incl. OpenAI-compat mode notes).
body:
## Context
DevEx is shipping production-minded Quickstart Templates (Python + TypeScript) for **RAG + agents**. Templates require: streaming, bounded retries/timeouts, tool calling, structured output validation, observability hooks, and safe defaults. A recurring open question in the requirements doc is the **final supported model pins for v1**.

This ticket defines:
- The **official supported model set** for v1 templates
- **Default pinned models** (what ships in `.env.example` / generated config)
- **Recommended upgrade path** (how users move to higher quality/throughput models)
- **Fallback policy** (when and how templates may gracefully degrade)

References:
- Confluence: “Template Requirements (v1): RAG + Agents Quickstarts” (Monica Patel)
- Confluence: “Provider Abstraction and Model Pinning” (Monica Patel)

---

## Decision summary (v1)
### A) Chat / agent model (required)
Templates MUST work with at least two Redwood-verified chat models:

**Default (ships in template config):**
- `rw://chat/redwood-verified/llama-3.1-8b-instruct@2025-02-10`

**Recommended production tier (documented in README):**
- `rw://chat/redwood-verified/llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-02-10`

Why two tiers:
- 8B provides a lower-cost, lower-latency default for “time-to-first-success” and internal testing.
- 70B provides better tool-calling and structured-output reliability for real workloads; we document how to switch.

Capability requirements for both tiers (must be met by Redwood serving profile):
- Streaming supported
- Tool calling supported (function/tool schema roundtrip)
- Template structured-output path works (native JSON mode or validated parsing)
- Stable request-id propagation (`redwood.request_id`), for supportability

### B) Embeddings model (required for RAG indexing)
**Default + supported embeddings pin:**
- `rw://embeddings/redwood-verified/bge-large-en@2025-01-05`

Notes:
- English-first is acceptable for v1 (matches sample docs + eval set). We’ll add multilingual guidance in v2 if demand warrants.
- Templates should keep embeddings swappable via config but only document this as the supported default for v1.

### C) Reranking model (optional in v1)
Reranking is NOT required for v1 success, but we will document an optional path (feature-flagged) and keep one supported pin for consistency:
- `rw://rerank/redwood-verified/bge-reranker-large@2025-01-12`

Guidance:
- Keep rerank off by default to reduce moving parts and cost.
- If enabled, rerank must have strict timeouts and be excluded from fallback logic (see below).

---

## Pinning guidance (what templates should do)
### What ships in `.env.example` / generated config
Templates should write pinned defaults at init time (or ship them checked in), and keep them readable:

Required:
- `RW_PROVIDER=redwood`
- `RW_MODEL=rw://chat/redwood-verified/llama-3.1-8b-instruct@2025-02-10`
- `RW_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL=rw://embeddings/redwood-verified/bge-large-en@2025-01-05`

Optional (documented but not required):
- `RW_MODEL_FALLBACKS=rw://chat/redwood-verified/llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-02-10`
  - See fallback policy section: this is only used on capacity-style failures.

README must include:
- “Why pinned?” explanation (reproducibility + supportability)
- “How to upgrade models” section (copy/paste replacements)
- “How to roll back” section (restore previous pin)

### OpenAI-compatible mode (docs guidance)
Templates may support `RW_PROVIDER=openai_compat`, but the docs should recommend Redwood-native mode as the default.

If OpenAI-compat is used:
- Prefer explicit `RW_OPENAI_COMPAT_MODEL` set by the user.
- If templates implement mapping from `RW_MODEL` -> compat model string, the mapping must be version-controlled and fail loudly with an actionable message.

---

## Fallback policy recommendations (conservative by default)
### Goals
- Keep apps online during capacity issues without hiding genuine correctness/config errors.
- Avoid surprising behavior (e.g., silent model changes) without clear observability signals.

### When fallback is allowed
Only attempt fallback when ALL are true:
1) The failure is classified as **capacity / upstream availability** (examples):
   - 503 “service unavailable”
   - explicit “capacity_exhausted” / “model_unavailable” style provider error
   - connection-level transient failures where retry budget is exhausted AND the error is marked retryable by the adapter
2) The request is safe to retry from the application perspective (templates: chat generation is safe to re-attempt if we have not streamed user-visible output yet).
3) We have not started streaming tokens to the client (no partial user-visible output).

### When fallback is NOT allowed
Do NOT fallback on:
- 401/403 auth errors
- 429 quota/rate-limit errors (fallback won’t help; it’s org-level)
- Tool schema / structured output validation failures
- User input errors (bad request)
- Retrieval empty results (that’s a data/index issue, not a model issue)

### How fallback should be surfaced (required observability)
If fallback occurs, templates MUST:
- Log a single structured event with:
  - `event=model_fallback`
  - `from_model=<pinned>`
  - `to_model=<fallback>`
  - `reason=<normalized error type/status>`
  - `redwood_request_id` if available
- Emit a counter metric (low-cardinality):
  - `rw.template.model_fallback.count{from_model,to_model,reason}`
- Add trace attribute on root span:
  - `rw.model_fallback=true`

### Default fallback recommendation for v1
- Fallback OFF by default (no `RW_MODEL_FALLBACKS` in `.env.example`).
- README includes a section “Enabling fallback (optional)” for production users who want graceful degradation.

Rationale:
- Keeps template behavior predictable during onboarding.
- Avoids obscuring errors during early debugging.
- Reduces operational surprises (silent quality changes).

---

## Rationale for model picks
- **llama-3.1-8b-instruct** as default: strong availability, low cost, fast TTFS for self-serve users; good enough for sample RAG + basic tools.
- **llama-3.1-70b-instruct** as recommended: improved instruction following and more robust tool calling/structured output; closer to “production-ready” expectations.
- **bge-large-en embeddings**: stable, widely understood baseline; good quality/cost tradeoff for template workloads.
- Optional **bge reranker**: provides a future lever for quality without changing the retrieval/indexing interface.

---

## Implementation notes for DevEx (what to change in templates)
- Ensure config schema includes BOTH chat + embeddings model pins (separate env vars) and validates that pins include a version segment (e.g., `@YYYY-MM-DD`).
- Ensure docs and comments call out that region/capacity tier should not be pinned by default.
- Ensure fallback logic is streaming-aware (no fallback after partial chunks are emitted).
- Ensure template eval harness runs with the default pins and records the pins in eval output metadata.

---

## Rollout / comms
- Update template READMEs to include:
  - “Supported models (v1)” table with the three pins above
  - “Choosing a model: dev vs production” guidance
  - “Fallback policy (optional)” with explicit do/don’t rules
- Provide a short snippet in docs-site walkthrough referencing the pins and linking to model pinning guidance.

---

## Open questions (tracked as follow-ups)
1) Do we want a second supported mid-tier chat model (e.g., ~30–40B) specifically for tool calling reliability at lower cost than 70B? If so, propose in v1.1.
2) Multilingual embeddings: wait for v2 unless a launch customer requires it.
3) For Dedicated/Private customers: confirm whether the same pinned identifiers work unchanged (expected) or whether Private catalogs require different ID formats.

---

## Final output for docs (copy/paste)
**Chat (default):** `rw://chat/redwood-verified/llama-3.1-8b-instruct@2025-02-10`
**Chat (recommended):** `rw://chat/redwood-verified/llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-02-10`
**Embeddings:** `rw://embeddings/redwood-verified/bge-large-en@2025-01-05`
**Rerank (optional):** `rw://rerank/redwood-verified/bge-reranker-large@2025-01-12`

Owner sign-off: Hosted API PM (Nikhil / Henry) + DevEx lead (Monica).
comments: 2025-02-24 (Henry Cho): Proposing two-tier chat support (8B default, 70B recommended). Need DevEx input on whether tool-calling reliability on 8B is sufficient for template smoke tests; if not, we can swap default to 70B but I’d like to avoid cost/429 issues for onboarding.

2025-02-26 (Monica Patel): Aligns with provider/pinning doc. +1 to fallback OFF by default; we’ve seen users struggle debugging when behavior changes. We’ll add a clearly documented opt-in env var for fallbacks and ensure it’s streaming-safe.

2025-03-03 (Allison Grant): Please ensure fallback emits a single metric with bounded cardinality (no request-specific tags). Add trace attribute on root span only; don’t attach error payloads as attributes.

2025-03-06 (Christine Wong): Fallback only pre-stream is critical. Also recommend we do not fallback on 429s; users should reduce concurrency / backoff instead. Include that explicitly in troubleshooting.
2025-03-18 (Nikhil Sharma): Approved. Please ensure docs call out that the recommended model for production is 70B and that cost controls (max output tokens) remain enabled when switching models.
